results.title: What is Inter-Coder Reliability? | Explanation & Strategies - ATLAS.ti
results.content: In qualitative research projects conducted by multiple researchers, inter-coder reliability is a standard reliability measure to ensure a research audience of the degree to which the analysis applied to qualitative data is consistent. In a nutshell, inter-coder reliability refers to the degree of agreement or consistency between two or more coders who are independently coding a set of data. If you have multiple coders looking at the data, demonstrating some measure of consistency or reliability of the coding can persuade your research audience that the codes and the subsequent analysis are credible. Inter-coder reliability, on the other hand, is more specific to qualitative research, where the 'coding' process involves categorizing or labeling data rather than scoring or rating it. Understanding inter-coder reliability begins with coding, a critical procedure where researchers transcribe, assemble and organize the raw data into manageable units that encapsulate the essence of that data. With each cycle, the understanding of the data deepens, the coding scheme becomes more refined, and the level of inter-coder reliability improves.

results.content: # What Is Bowenian Family and Couples Therapy? * Bowenian therapy focuses on understanding family dynamics to foster emotional growth & resolve relational issues. This article will describe how to use the concepts and techniques of Bowenian Therapy to help a family resolve conflict and aid individual family members in achieving emotional independence. * What Is Bowenian Family and Couples Therapy? ## What Is Bowenian Family and Couples Therapy? In his work with mothers and children, Bowen began to develop his theory of differentiation of self, which would become a cornerstone of his family systems theory. But Bowen believed emotional cutoff led to problems in relationships outside of the family. A person who has an unresolved conflict with their family is at risk of making their outside relationships too important and creating substitute families within their work or current relationships (The Bowen Center, n.d.). In a family therapy intervention, the therapist would identify triangulation and see how the dynamic is playing out between Michael, Rose, and Frank. An important technique used in Bowenian Family Therapy is the use of process questions (The Bowen Center, n.d.). Another process question may be to ask Rose how she is creating distance between herself and her family. A final technique used in Bowenian Family Therapy is *coaching*. One important tool in Bowenian Family Therapy is teaching clients how to use “I” statements when communicating. In Bowenian Therapy, the family attempts to develop new processes to see how the dynamics at home can change. ### Working with emotionally cutoff family members. One way to increase self-differentiation and reduce triangulation is to foster more direct communication between certain family members. But, it is normal and common for families to struggle with conflict, and Bowenian Therapy can help. Bowenian therapy examines family patterns across generations to identify and change dysfunctional behaviors. Techniques like genograms (family trees) and process questions help individuals understand their roles and improve communication within the family system. Key concepts include differentiation of self (maintaining personal identity), emotional triangles (relationship dynamics), family projection process (transmission of emotional issues), multigenerational transmission process (passing down patterns), and societal emotional process (societal influences on family functioning).
